headline: Seven majors sit below their 200-day lines while fear sits at 27, and the tape's flows don't agree with each other either
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles everything else. All seven assets on this board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, trade below their 200-day moving average with no golden crosses anywhere. That's not a mixed market, it's a uniform one. The distance from 12-month highs tells you how far the retracement runs: BTC is 49% off its high of $124,773.51, ETH is down 60.6% from $4,829.23, and the small caps are worse, DOGE at -75.7% and ADA at -83.2%. When every asset in the book sits under its long-run trendline, you're not picking through a rotation, you're reading a broad drawdown.

Momentum tells a more interesting story than trend alone. RSI-14 readings cluster in neutral territory (BTC 47.4, ETH 56.3, SOL 42.7, ADA 46.1), which means nothing is technically oversold or overbought despite the trend damage. MACD is split: BNB and DOGE sit above their signal lines even while priced below their 200-day averages, a short-term momentum flicker inside a longer downtrend. ETH is the clearer divergence: RSI at 56.3, up 1.81% over 7 days and 6.36% over 30 days, all while still 60.6% off its high and below its 200-day line. That's a coin catching a bid without yet repairing the bigger picture, worth naming precisely because the daily (-0.78%), weekly, and monthly numbers point in different directions.

Positioning is where the crowd's bet gets priced. Funding is negative on BTC (-2.0% annualized) and DOGE (-2.9%), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position, a costly stance for the bears. Funding runs positive on ETH (1.8%), SOL (4.2%), and XRP (11.0%), so longs are paying there instead. Yet long/short account ratios lean long everywhere, sharply so on DOGE (4.98) and XRP (3.22). Recent liquidations lean toward longs getting hurt: BTC saw $5.26M in long liquidations against $3.67M in shorts over 23 hours, ETH $11.48M longs versus $6.71M shorts over 19 hours. Crowded long positioning paying to stay long, and getting liquidated more than shorts, is the kind of setup that reads fragile rather than comfortable.

Flows show real disagreement. BTC spot ETFs printed -$265.4M on 31 Jul, with the five-session net at -$61.5M and same_direction_days at just 1, so call that one heavy day, not a run. ETH ETFs went the other way, +$9.0M on 31 Jul with a +$10.0M five-session net and two same-direction days, a small but slightly more consistent bid. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is down 1.59% over 30 days to $303.8B, so the sidelines cash pool is shrinking, not growing. Whale activity over the last 48 hours nets $15.3M moving off exchanges overall, but split by asset: BTC saw $23.97M net leave exchanges while ETH saw $8.63M net arrive at exchanges (Coinbase Institutional took in $68.3M of it). The weekly net figures over the last four periods ($728.3M, -$146.9M, $445.9M, $723.7M) show three of four leaning toward exchange outflows, though the pattern isn't a straight line.

Set that against sentiment: Fear & Greed reads 27, squarely in Fear, sitting mid-range within its own 30-day band of 20 to 33. So the crowd feels fearful while BTC is quietly leaving exchanges in size and DOGE's funding pays longs to hold shorts. That gap between mood and metal is the day's real tension, not a signal to act on, just a fact to sit with.

What's worth watching from here: whether BTC's ETF flow finds a second same-direction day (it's at 1 now) to turn a single print into an actual trend, whether funding on BTC and DOGE flips positive as crowded long ratios meet negative funding, and whether any of the seven majors reclaims its 200-day line, which would be the first real break in an otherwise uniform below-trend picture.
